question.text: This man rose to power during the Reign of Terror as leader of the Committee of Public Safety. He was executed during the Thermidorean Reaction.
question.clue: This man denounced the practitioners of the Religion of Reason, the Hebertists, and instead attempted to establish a religion of the Supreme Being.

swap.text: English forces under Henry V utilized the longbow during this battle, which took place during St. Crispin's Day. During this battle, French forces under Charles d'Albret got stuck in muddy terrain.
swap.clue: "Double subsidies" raised a fleet of up to 1,500 cogs for the winners of this battle, who attempted to retreat to Calais after taking heavy losses while besieging Harfleur.

question.text: The name Operation Overlord referred to this event that included five beach landing points and took place on June 6, 1944.
question.answerHtml: D-Day [or anything referring to the Allied invasion of Normandy]
question.clue: Participants in this event move away from the camera in the photo Into the Jaws of Death.

swap.leadin: Cardinal Richelieu besieged members of this group at La Rochelle. --.
swap.text: Name this religious group whose freedom of worship was granted by the Edict of Nantes and revoked by the Edict of Fontainebleau.
swap.clue: These people were welcomed into Prussia via the Edict of Potsdam.

question.text: This final French emperor was captured by the Germans at the Battle of Sedan, after which he was forced to abdicate his throne. He shares his name with his uncle, who ruled France from 1804 to 1815.
question.clue: Together with Camilo Cavour, this man concluded the secret agreement of Plombiers, and assistance to the Piedmontese in the victory over Austria at the Battle of Solferino resulted in the Peace of Villafranca.

swap.leadin: This ruler defeated Odo of Aquitaine at the Battle of Soissons, though he later fought alongside Odo against an Umayyad invasion led by Abd-ar-Rahman.
swap.text: Identify this ruler who defeated a Muslim army at the Battle of Tours. This ruler's son Pepin the Short became a king following the deposition of Childeric III.
swap.clue: He supported the missionary work of St. Boniface, and was imprisoned by his father's widow Plectrude.

question.leadin: This people was divided into two primary groups: the Ripuarians and the Salians.
question.text: Name this Germanic people that gives their name to the modern-day nation that contains the city of Marseilles.
question.clue: Fantasia meant "stubbornness" or "arrogance" in a system of speech named for this word that was often used in a type of prison called a bagnio ("BAN-yo").

swap.text: After Richelieu's death, the French nobility, allied with peasants and other factions, engaged in two rebellions against the monarchy collectively given this name. It is French for "sling," which rebels used to smash windows.
swap.clue: That commander's greatest victory came at the Battle of Blanc-Champ in spite of a dispute between the Picardie regiment and the Gardes francaises that gave Turenne an opening.

question.leadin: Snoopy always fought against the Red Baron. Answer these questions on World War I.
question.text: This engagement lasted from February to July of 1916 in which General Petain stalled the advance of General von Falkenhayn. 400,000 French and as many Germans lost their lives.
question.clue: One of the primary French commanders at this engagement, Robert Nivelle, declared "They shall not pass!"

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the revolutions of 1848.
swap.text: The February Revolution in France brought down this final French king and successor to Charles X.
swap.answerHtml: Louis Philippe I [or Louis Philippe III, Duke of Orleans]
swap.clue: The September Laws were passed after Giuseppe Fieschi killed 18 people around this man with a twenty-barreled monster weapon called the "infernal machine."

question.leadin: This university was the second oldest in Europe, founded after Bologna but predating both Oxford and Cambridge.
question.text: Name this university whose alumni included Jean Calvin, Denis Diderot, Voltaire and Honore de Balzac. It was located in the Sorbonne district of its namesake city.
question.clue: It gave control of one of its colleges to the Dutch proto-reformer Jan Standonck, and in the Reformation it graduated Erasmus, Calvin, and John Knox.

swap.leadin: The assassination of Archduke Ferdinand may have been one of the precipitating causes of World War I, but it certainly wasn't the only one. answer the following about the events leading up to the Great War.
swap.text: One of the major factors was simmering feelings on both sides after the Franco-Prussian War. All or nothing, the French were especially annoyed that Germany ended up with these two iron rich-regions in the northeast at the war's conclusion.
swap.clue: This two territories that France ceded to the Germans after its defeat in the Franco-Prussian War.

question.text: Colbert directly pushed for the creation of the Royal Manufacture on the Glass of Mirrors, whose main purpose was to prevent the usage of imported Venetian Glass in the construction of this palace's Hall of Mirrors.
question.clue: The unification ceremony for Germany occurred here, and a bread shortage led women to march to it on October 5, 1789.

swap.text: This treaty was signed in 1802 by Joseph Bonaparte and Marquess Cornwallis as a "definitive treaty of peace" between France and England. Hostilities resumed in slightly more than a year.
swap.clue: The Republic of the Seven Ionian Islands achieved recognition as a result of this treaty, and under it Egypt was taken from France and restored to the Ottoman Empire under British supervision.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the world's third-most famous Renaissance.
question.text: A "Renaissance" of scholarship occurred during the rule of this Frankish dynasty, whose name derives from that of the victor at the Battle of Tours. Its rulers included Pepin the Short and Louis the Pious.
question.clue: Another king standardized succession rules with his Ordinatio imperii.

swap.text: Two younger brothers of Lothair legitimized their alliance with this document, which contains early specimens of Old High German and Romance vernaculars.
swap.clue: This pact of alliance between Louis the German and Charles the Bald. Recorded in three languages, including Old French, it is the first surviving use of a written French vernacular.

question.text: This author of the Nouvelles meditations poetiques became the de facto head of the Second Republic following the February Revolution. He declared that France "will make no secret propagation or incendiarism among its neighbors" in his "Manifesto to Europe".
question.clue: This major advocate of the tricoleur helped organize the Second Republic in meetings at the Hotel de Ville and served as its Minister of Foreign Affairs. He wrote an influential 1847 History of the Girondins ("jee-ron-DANS").

swap.leadin: This school inspired the intendant Pierre Poivre ("pwahv") to conserve forests in an attempt to halt plantation erosion and provide rainfall for smuggled spice gardens.
swap.text: Name this economic school that guided 18th-century French exploitation of natural wealth in the Mascarenes.
swap.answerHtml: physiocrats [or physiocracy or physiocratic school; prompt on economistes] (The tongue twister “Peter Piper” may reference Poivre bringing spices to Mauritius, Réunion, and the Seychelles.)
swap.clue: Believing that mercantilist legislation and government regulations actually hampered the expansion of trade, this group believed that land is the source of all wealth. For 15 points-name this French school of economists which included Pierre Dupont de Nemours and Francois Quesnay.

question.text: This position, held by a man who ordered the Massacre at Vassy, was also held by a man who plotted the assassination of Gaspard de Coligny along with Catherine de Medici.

swap.leadin: This faction formed when Charles of Orleans married the daughter of Bernard VII; it opposed John the Fearless who was assassinated and succeeded by his son Philip the Good. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this French faction which fought a civil war in the early 1400s with the Burgundians.
